problems.title: Sharp bounds for two expressions
problems.question: 3≤m≤7 and 5≤n≤8. Bound 2m−3n and (5m+7n)/(mn).
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Use endpoint monotonicity; the fraction equals 5/n+7/m.
steps: The first is smallest at (m,n)=(3,8), giving −18, and largest at (7,5), giving −1.
The second decreases as either positive variable increases: its minimum is 5/8+7/7=13/8 and maximum 5/5+7/3=10/3. All endpoints are attained.

problems.title: A rational equation reduced to one ratio
problems.question: Solve $3/(2x+1)^2+4/(2x+5)^2=7/[(2x+1)(2x+5)]$.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: Multiply by (2x+5)² to get 3t²−7t+4=(3t−4)(t−1)=0.
t=1 would imply 5=1 and is impossible. For t=4/3, 3(2x+5)=4(2x+1), giving x=11/2. This is allowed.

problems.question: Solve (4x+1)/3−(19−x)/2>x.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Multiply by positive 6 to preserve the inequality.

problems.title: Two branches and a sign check
problems.question: Solve |5x+7|=2x+9.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: The positive case gives x=2/3. The negative case gives x=−16/7.
Both satisfy x≥−9/2 and directly satisfy the absolute-value equation.

problems.title: A triangle defined by three inequalities
problems.question: Shade the solution of y≤2x−3, x+y≤9, 5y−x≥3.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Intersect the boundary lines; use closed half-planes because the inequalities include equality.
steps: The three pairwise intersections are (2,1), (4,5), (7,2). Each satisfies the remaining inequality.
The solution is the filled triangle with those vertices, including its three edges: above y=(x+3)/5 and below both upper lines.

problems.title: When an intersection of open intervals is empty
problems.question: For which a is x>a, x>2, x<a+3 unsolvable?
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: The allowed interval is (max(a,2),a+3), nonempty iff its left endpoint is smaller.
steps: a<a+3 always. Thus the only further requirement for existence is 2<a+3, or a>−1.
Its complement, including the equality case with touching open endpoints, is a≤−1.

problems.title: A quadrilateral formed from two medians
problems.question: ABC is right with hypotenuse AB=30. Medians AN,BM meet at O; K,P are midpoints of AO,BO. Find perimeter KPNM.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Triangle midsegment theorem and the centroid’s 2:1 division.
steps: K=(2u/3,v/6),P=(u/6,2v/3). Distances give KP=MN=30/2=15 and PN=MK=30/6=5.
The perimeter is 15+5+15+5=40.

problems.title: Ratios at the intersection of two cevians
problems.question: N lies on AC with AN:NC=4:9; M lies on BC with BM:MC=2:7. AM and BN meet at O. Find AO:OM and BO:ON.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Mass-point balancing: endpoint masses are inverse to the division ratio; masses add at a division point.
steps: Assign masses A=9,C=4 to balance N. To balance M use B=14, since B:C=7:2.
Then M has mass 18 and N mass 13. Along AM the ratio AO:OM=18:9=2:1; along BN, BO:ON=13:14.

problems.title: Point power and a radius-length chord
problems.question: An exterior point is √7 from a circle centre. Its secant has inside length r equal to the radius and outside length 2r. Find r.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Power of a point: external × whole = centre distance squared − radius squared.
steps: (2r)(3r)=7−r² gives 7r²=7. The positive radius is 1.

problems.title: A tangential trapezoid with a known diagonal
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 3,12, a diagonal 6, and an incircle. Find the inradius.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Tangential quadrilateral: leg sum = base sum; height equals 2r.
steps: Put A=(0,0),D=(12,0),B=(x,h),C=(x+3,h) and choose AC=6 by reflection if necessary. Let t=x+3, so h²=36−t².
The leg squares are AB²=(t−3)²+h²=45−6t and CD²=(12−t)²+h²=180−24t=4AB².
Thus CD=2AB. Their sum is 15, so AB=5,CD=10. From 25=45−6t obtain t=10/3.
